#TECNO #SPARK40Series #SPARK40 #TECNOAI
hook_text: SPARK 40 16GB+256GB and the price 16,499 (Taka) printed on the poster from frame 0
first_3s: A finished product poster as video: TECNO logo top-left, 'SPARK 40' and '16GB+256GB' in big blue type, the phone shown front and back, the price strip under it. Nothing moves except a slow push on the phone.

structure.what: static poster: model name, memory size, phone render, price 16,499 + VAT all visible the whole time; the phone render nudges forward once
black end card with the TECNO wordmark

camera: none, graphic poster with a slow push
visual_style: flat poster, pale blue gradient, product render in a glass panel
text_style: dark navy bold sans for the name, blue gradient for the memory size, price large under the phone, all centred in the upper and lower thirds
music_mood: none heard (no music track on the poster video)
cta: none on screen; the channel and title carry the offer
why_viral: A clean brand poster with the price in frame 0 reached 700K views on a 26K-subscriber channel because the brand's regional channel is fed to Shorts like an ad and the price makes it concrete.
lesson_for_engine: A price-banner poster Short (model, key spec, price, one slow push, end card) is the cheapest honest format a Rwandan phone shop can copy.

caption:
Can you believe this is in Kenya? 🇮🇳🇰🇪 #Kenya #IndianFood #Yummy
#India in #Kenya

Despite experiencing and loving all the experiences in
new countries, both Ankit and I long for our homes and
sense of belongingness.

This particular area felt like a time travel, where even
though momentarily, it felt like we are back to India.

Location - Diamond Plaza, Nairobi
hook_text: Mini India in Kenya (title card on screen for the whole clip)
first_3s: A woman in a yellow top walks past mannequins in a mall shop; a white label 'Mini India (flag) in Kenya (flag)' sits at the top of the frame and stays there.

structure.what: walking shot in an Indian clothes shop in a Nairobi mall, label on screen
shopfront of Bhajia Point, she turns to camera
cook assembling pani puri at the counter, then she eats them at a pink tray
pointing at a copper pot of curry
a jewellery and spices shop, she walks in

camera: handheld, follows her from behind and in selfie
visual_style: mall interior and street, natural and shop light
text_style: white rounded box, black sans text, top centre, same on every shot
why_viral: A one-line surprise title that is true of the next 15 seconds; Kenyans and Indians in Kenya both commented to claim it.
lesson_for_engine: Put one curiosity line at the top for the whole clip and show five quick places or dishes under it; shops can copy it as 'everything in our shop in 15 seconds'.

top_comments.text: As an indian living in kenya, I couldn't believe it too! 😭❤️
Omg I’m from Kenya Nairobi I’m so happy my country gets respect
Diamond plaza ofcourse...👍
Wakenya ambia huyu dem aende base ya smocha
Diamond plaza in kanairo thanks for the video😊

notes: Creator channel based in India, filmed in Nairobi; counted as Kenya because of the location.

caption:
Grilled Chicken War in Uganda! #StreetFood #Uganda #CultureShock
grilled chicken war in uganda!

#unique #viralvideo #videoviral #viralshorts #education
hook_text: Roadside vendors push skewers of grilled chicken into the car window (words appear one at a time: MIGHT OF TAKE TO MINE UGANDA)
first_3s: A very muscular vendor walks to a car window holding two bundles of chicken skewers; a word pops up in the middle of the frame with each cut.

structure.what: vendor approaches the car window with skewers, first captioned word
skewers shoved in at passengers, a woman grimaces, a man laughs; more vendors arrive
car interior full of chicken, hands reaching in from every side, last words 'Uganda'

visual_style: red dirt road, car interior, daylight
text_style: white italic heavy sans with black outline, one word at a time, lower middle of the frame
why_viral: A real roadside scene played as a comedy: the escalation (more hands, more chicken) is clear with no sound, and the one-word captions keep the eye moving.
lesson_for_engine: A street-food seller's busiest moment, filmed from the customer's seat with a one-word caption per cut, is a copyable hook for restaurants.

top_comments.text: This chickens are the most delicious chicken the organic by the way😂😂😂
Looks delicious

This happened to me in Kenya on the way to Watamu either way ppl do it all over the world😊
If that first bloke offered me grilled chicken I wouldn't dare say no 💪🏼💪🏼

notes: Creator channel with a US base; content is a Ugandan roadside scene (search 'Uganda business').

caption: Everything you can get with $1 in Nairobi, Kenya
hook_text: What you can get with $1 in Nairobi, Kenya (he holds up a dollar bill)
first_3s: The host stands in a Nairobi street holding a one-dollar note to camera, a black title box over it; then straight to a mandazi in his hand.

structure.what: host with the $1 note, title box, selfie speech
mandazi at 0 of 130 Ksh, masala chai at 20/130, walking to Muthurwa market at 40/130
matatu short trip 60/130, then ugali and sukuma 110/130
mayai pasua (boiled egg) and more street snacks
back to selfie holding the chai, counter at 130/130 Ksh, 'that's what you can get on the streets of Nairobi'

camera: selfie stick plus handheld street shots
visual_style: street food stalls, market, matatus, daylight
on_screen_text: What you can get with $1 in Nairobi, Kenya
text_style: white bold sans with soft shadow, a running price counter lower middle and a small caption line above it
voice: host in English narrating each item
why_viral: A budget challenge with a counter that fills up gives a built-in progress bar; Kenyans piled into the comments to correct, tease and laugh (2.1K comments).
lesson_for_engine: A running price counter (0/130 to 130/130) is a hook and a progress bar at once; a shop can run it as 'what 5,000 RWF buys here'.

caption: Brazilian wool #braidhairstylesforblackwomen #hairstyle #geecurlysalon
hook_text: Close-up of a stylist's gloved hands crocheting wool into long twists (the title names the style)
first_3s: Orange-gloved hands with pink nails pull a crochet hook through a section of twisted hair; the sectioned scalp pattern is bright orange against dark hair.

structure.what: hands install the wool twists section by section, same camera angle
the finished long twists hang down the back, camera pulls back a little

camera: handheld, over the stylist's shoulder, vertical
visual_style: salon interior, ring light, other clients in the background
text_style: no text on screen; the style name is only in the title
music_mood: trending sound is not heard (muted watch) per the channel's usual reels
cta: none in video; location is in the channel description (Roysambu)
why_viral: A satisfying process shot with a clear result and no talking; viewers save the style and ask where the salon is and how many packs of wool were used.
lesson_for_engine: A salon's best Short is the process close-up of one hairstyle with the name in the title; add the area and a number only in a text line.
